translations.idiomatic: On a renzi day, if the four horizons are clear except for red banner-clouds with troops rising beneath them—or spread in all directions—war engulfs the realm.

sentences.zh: 若四望無雲，獨見黑雲極天，天下兵大起。

translations.literal: If in the four vistas there are no clouds, alone seeing black clouds filling heaven—great warfare rises throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: If the four horizons are cloudless except for black vapor filling the sky, war rises on a vast scale.

sentences.zh: 半天，半起。

translations.literal: Half the sky—half rise.
translations.idiomatic: Half the sky covered means war in half the realm.

sentences.zh: 三日內有雨，災解。

translations.literal: If rain comes within three days, the disaster is resolved.
translations.idiomatic: Rain within three days lifts the omen.

sentences.zh: 敵欲來者，其氣上有雲，下有氛零，中天而下，敵必至。

translations.literal: If the enemy is about to come, their qi has clouds above and scattered mist below, descending from mid-heaven—the enemy is certain to arrive.
translations.idiomatic: When foes approach, their vapor shows clouds above and scattered mist below descending from mid-heaven—the enemy will arrive.

sentences.zh: 雲氣如旌旗，賊兵暴起。

translations.literal: Cloud-qi like banners and flags—bandit armies rise suddenly.
translations.idiomatic: Banner-like cloud-vapor means bandit armies rise suddenly.

sentences.zh: 暴兵氣，如人持刀楯，雲如人，赤色，所臨城邑，有卒兵至，驚怖，須臾去。

translations.literal: Sudden-army qi like men holding shields, clouds like men, red in color—the city or town they overspread has soldiers arriving; terror, then they swiftly depart.
translations.idiomatic: Sudden-army vapor like shield-bearing men, red man-shaped clouds over a town, means raiders arrive, terrify the place, and quickly leave.

sentences.zh: 赤氣如人持節，兵來未息。

translations.literal: Red qi like a man holding an insignia—warfare comes and has not ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Red vapor like a man bearing an insignia of office means war continues without end.

sentences.zh: 雲如方虹，有暴兵。

translations.literal: Clouds like a square rainbow—sudden armies rise.
translations.idiomatic: Square-rainbow clouds mean sudden armies.

sentences.zh: 赤雲如火者，所向兵至。

translations.literal: Red clouds like fire—where they point, armies arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Fire-red clouds mark wherever armies will march.

sentences.zh: 天有白氣，狀如匹布，經醜未者，天下多兵。

translations.literal: Heaven has white qi shaped like a bolt of cloth, passing through chou and wei—warfare is widespread throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: White cloth-like vapor crossing the chou and wei quarters means war throughout the land.

sentences.zh: 凡戰氣，青白如膏，將勇。

translations.literal: In general, battle-qi green-white like paste—the general is brave.
translations.idiomatic: Green-white paste-like battle vapor marks a brave commander.

sentences.zh: 大戰氣，如人無頭，如死人臥。

translations.literal: Great-battle qi like headless men, like dead men lying down.
translations.idiomatic: Great-battle vapor shaped like headless or prostrate corpses.

sentences.zh: 敵上氣如丹蛇，赤氣隨之，必大戰，殺將。

translations.literal: Enemy upper qi like a cinnabar serpent, with red qi following—great battle is certain, and generals are killed.
translations.idiomatic: Cinnabar serpent vapor above the enemy, trailing red qi, means great battle and dead generals.

sentences.zh: 四望無雲，見赤氣如狗入營，其下有流血。

translations.literal: In the four vistas with no clouds, seeing red qi like a dog entering camp—below there is flowing blood.
translations.idiomatic: Clear skies except for red dog-vapor entering camp mean bloodshed below.

sentences.zh: 凡連陰十日，晝不見日，夜不見月，亂風四起，欲雨而無雨，名曰蒙，臣謀君。

translations.literal: In general, continuous overcast for ten days—by day the sun is not seen, by night the moon is not seen; chaotic winds rise on four sides; rain is expected but does not fall—this is called meng; ministers plot against the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Ten days of overcast with invisible sun and moon, wild winds, and promised rain that never falls is called meng—ministers plot against the throne.

sentences.zh: 故曰，久陰不雨臣謀主。

translations.literal: Therefore it is said: long overcast without rain means ministers plot against the lord.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the saying: prolonged cloud cover without rain means ministers conspire against their sovereign.

sentences.zh: 霧氣若晝若夜，其色青黃，更相掩冒，乍合乍散，臣謀君，逆者喪。

translations.literal: Fog-qi like day and like night, its colors green and yellow, mutually covering and hiding, now joining now dispersing—ministers plot against the ruler; rebels perish.
translations.idiomatic: Day-night fog shifting green and yellow, merging and breaking, means ministerial plots—and doomed rebels.

sentences.zh: 山中冬霧十日不解者，欲崩之候。

translations.literal: Winter fog in the mountains not clearing for ten days—sign of impending collapse.
translations.idiomatic: Mountain winter fog lasting ten days signals imminent collapse.

sentences.zh: 視四方常有大雲，五色具者，其下有賢人隱也。

translations.literal: Looking in the four directions, there are always great clouds with all five colors complete—below them a worthy man is in hiding.
translations.idiomatic: Great five-colored clouds always visible in the four directions mean a worthy man hides below.

sentences.zh: 青雲潤澤蔽日，在西北為舉賢良。

translations.literal: Green clouds moist and lustrous veiling the sun, in the northwest—raising worthy and good men.
translations.idiomatic: Moist green clouds veiling the sun in the northwest mean worthy men will be elevated.

sentences.zh: 雲氣如亂穰，大風將至，視所從來避之。

translations.literal: Cloud-qi like tangled hemp—great wind is about to come; watch whence it comes and avoid it.
translations.idiomatic: Tangled-hemp cloud-vapor means a great wind is coming—watch its origin and take shelter.

sentences.zh: 雲甚潤而厚，大雨必暴至。

translations.literal: Clouds very moist and thick—violent great rain is certain to arrive suddenly.
translations.idiomatic: Very moist, thick clouds promise a sudden downpour.

sentences.zh: 四始之日，有黑雲氣如陣，厚重大者，多雨。

translations.literal: On the four beginning days, black cloud-qi like a battle line, thick and heavy—much rain.
translations.idiomatic: On the four seasonal beginnings, heavy black battle-line clouds mean heavy rain.

sentences.zh: 氣若霧非霧，衣冠不雨而濡，見則其城帶甲而趣。

translations.literal: Qi like fog yet not fog—caps and robes wet without rain; when seen, that city girds in armor and hurries forth.
translations.idiomatic: Fog-like vapor that wets clothing without rain means the city below arms and marches out.

sentences.zh: 日出沒時，有雲橫截之，白者喪，烏者驚。

translations.literal: At sunrise and sunset, clouds cross and cut across—white means mourning; black means alarm.
translations.idiomatic: Clouds cutting across the sun at dawn or dusk: white means mourning, black alarm.

sentences.zh: 三日內雨者各解。

translations.literal: If rain comes within three days, each omen is resolved.
translations.idiomatic: Rain within three days clears each omen.

sentences.zh: 有黑氣入營者，兵相殘。

translations.literal: Black qi entering camp—armies mutually slaughter one another.
translations.idiomatic: Black vapor entering camp means armies turn on one another.

sentences.zh: 有赤青氣入營者，兵弱。

translations.literal: Red and green qi entering camp—armies are weak.
translations.idiomatic: Red and green vapor entering camp weakens the army.

sentences.zh: 有雲如蛟龍，所見處將軍失魄。

translations.literal: Clouds like horned dragons—where seen, generals lose their souls.
translations.idiomatic: Dragon clouds wherever seen mean generals lose heart.

sentences.zh: 有雲如鵠尾，來廕國上，三日亡。

translations.literal: Clouds like a wild-goose tail, coming to shade the state—within three days it perishes.
translations.idiomatic: Wild-goose-tail clouds shading the capital mean destruction within three days.

sentences.zh: 有雲如日月暈，赤色，其國凶。

translations.literal: Clouds like solar and lunar halos, red in color—the state is ill-fated.
translations.idiomatic: Red halo-like clouds mean ill fortune for the state.

sentences.zh: 青白色，有大水。

translations.literal: Green-white color—great flood.
translations.idiomatic: Green-white color foretells great floods.

sentences.zh: 有雲狀如龍行，國有大水，人流亡。

translations.literal: Clouds shaped like a dragon moving—the state has great flood, people flee and wander.
translations.idiomatic: Dragon-moving clouds mean great floods and wandering refugees.

sentences.zh: 有雲赤黃色，四塞終日，竟夜照地者，大臣縱恣。

translations.literal: Clouds red and yellow, blocking all four quarters all day, shining on the ground all night—great ministers act without restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Red-yellow clouds sealing the four quarters day and night mean great ministers run unchecked.

sentences.zh: 有雲如氣，昧而濁，賢人去，小人在位。

translations.literal: Clouds like qi, dim and turbid—worthy men depart, petty men hold office.
translations.idiomatic: Dim, turbid cloud-vapor means worthy men leave and petty men take office.

sentences.zh: 凡白虹者，百殃之本，眾亂所基。

translations.literal: In general, white rainbows are the root of a hundred calamities, the foundation of mass disorder.
translations.idiomatic: White rainbows are the root of countless calamities and the seed of rebellion.

sentences.zh: 霧者，眾邪之氣，陰來冒陽。

translations.literal: Fog is the qi of many evils; yin comes to overwhelm yang.
translations.idiomatic: Fog is the vapor of many evils—yin pressing down upon yang.

sentences.zh: 凡遇四方盛氣，無向之戰。

translations.literal: In general, when encountering flourishing qi in the four directions, do not give battle facing toward it.
translations.idiomatic: Never fight facing the flourishing qi of any quarter.

sentences.zh: 甲乙日青氣在東方，丙丁日赤氣在南方，庚辛日白氣在西方，壬癸日黑氣在北方，戊巳日黃氣在中央。

translations.literal: On jia and yi days green qi is in the east; on bing and ding days red qi in the south; on geng and xin days white qi in the west; on ren and gui days black qi in the north; on wu and ji days yellow qi in the center.
translations.idiomatic: On jia/yi days green qi fills the east; bing/ding, red in the south; geng/xin, white in the west; ren/gui, black in the north; wu/ji, yellow at the center.

sentences.zh: 四季戰當此日氣，背之吉。

translations.literal: Battles in the four seasons on days of this qi—turning the back to it is auspicious.
translations.idiomatic: In seasonal battles on such days, fighting with your back to that qi is auspicious.

sentences.zh: 日中有黑氣，君有小過而臣不諫，又掩君惡而揚君善，故日中有黑氣不明也。

translations.literal: Black qi within the sun—the ruler has small faults and ministers do not remonstrate; moreover they cover the ruler's faults and proclaim the ruler's virtues—therefore black qi within the sun makes it not bright.
translations.idiomatic: Black vapor in the sun means the ruler errs slightly while ministers flatter instead of remonstrating, hiding faults and praising virtues—hence the sun dims.

sentences.zh: 凡白虹霧，奸臣謀君，擅權立威。

translations.literal: In general, white rainbows and fog—treacherous ministers plot against the ruler and usurp authority to establish power.
translations.idiomatic: White rainbows and fog mean treacherous ministers plot against the throne and seize power.

sentences.zh: 晝霧夜明，臣志得申，夜霧晝明，臣志不申。

translations.literal: Day fog and bright night—ministers' aims succeed; night fog and bright day—ministers' aims fail.
translations.idiomatic: Day fog with bright night lets ministers succeed; night fog with bright day blocks them.

sentences.zh: 霧終日終時，君有憂。

translations.literal: Fog lasting a whole day or whole period—the ruler has sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: Fog lasting a full day or watch brings the ruler sorrow.

sentences.zh: 色黃小雨。

translations.literal: Yellow color—small rain.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow color means light rain.

sentences.zh: 白言兵喪，青言疾，黑有暴水，赤有兵喪，黃言土功，或有大風。

translations.literal: White speaks of military mourning; green of illness; black of sudden flood; red of military mourning; yellow of earthworks, or great wind.
translations.idiomatic: White signals military losses; green, disease; black, sudden floods; red, military mourning; yellow, public works or great wind.

sentences.zh: 凡夜霧，白虹見，臣有憂。

translations.literal: In general, night fog with white rainbow appearing—ministers have sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: Night fog with a white rainbow means sorrow for ministers.

sentences.zh: 晝霧白虹見，君有憂。

translations.literal: Day fog with white rainbow appearing—the ruler has sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: Day fog with a white rainbow means sorrow for the ruler.

sentences.zh: 虹頭尾至地，流血之象。

translations.literal: Rainbow head and tail reaching the ground—image of flowing blood.
translations.idiomatic: A rainbow whose head and tail touch the ground foretells bloodshed.

sentences.zh: 凡霧氣不順四時，逆相交錯，微風小雨，為陰陽氣亂之象。

translations.literal: In general, fog-qi not conforming to the four seasons, contrary and crossing—light wind and small rain—image of yin and yang qi in disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Season-defying fog with crossing winds and drizzle shows yin and yang in disorder.

sentences.zh: 從寅至辰巳上，周而復始，為逆者不成。

translations.literal: From yin to chen and si above, cycling and repeating—rebels do not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Fog cycling from yin through chen and si means rebels fail.

sentences.zh: 積日不解，晝夜昏暗，天下欲分離。

translations.literal: Accumulating for days without clearing, day and night dim— the realm wishes to split apart.
translations.idiomatic: Days of unbroken dim fog mean the realm is splitting apart.

sentences.zh: 凡霧四合，有虹各見其方，隨四時色吉，非時色凶。

translations.literal: In general, fog gathering on four sides, rainbows each visible in their quarter—following seasonal colors is auspicious; colors out of season are inauspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Fog on all sides with rainbows in each quarter: seasonal colors are lucky; unseasonal colors, ill.

sentences.zh: 氣色青黃，更相掩覆，乍合乍散，臣欲謀君，為逆者不成，自亡。

translations.literal: Qi colors green and yellow, mutually covering, now joining now dispersing—ministers wish to plot against the ruler; rebels do not succeed and destroy themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Green-yellow vapor merging and breaking means ministerial plots—and self-destructing rebels.

sentences.zh: 凡霧氣四方俱起，百步不見人，名曰晝昏，不有破國，必有滅門。

translations.literal: In general, fog-qi rising on all four sides, men not visible at a hundred paces—called day-darkness; if there is not a broken state, there is certain destruction of a clan.
translations.idiomatic: Fog on all four sides with visibility under a hundred paces is "day-darkness"—if no state falls, a clan is wiped out.

sentences.zh: 凡天地四方昏濛若下塵，十日五日以上，或一日，或一時，雨不沾衣而有土，名曰霾。

translations.literal: In general, heaven and earth on four sides dim and hazy as if dust falls—for ten or five days or more, or one day, or one period; rain does not wet clothing yet there is dust—called mai.
translations.idiomatic: Haze like falling dust for days on end, rain that does not wet clothes yet leaves grit—this is mai.

sentences.zh: 故曰，天地霾，君臣乖，大旱。

translations.literal: Therefore it is said: heaven and earth in mai—ruler and ministers estranged; great drought.
translations.idiomatic: Hence: heaven and earth in mai mean estranged ruler and ministers and great drought.

sentences.zh: 凡海傍蜃氣象樓臺，廣野氣成宮闕，北夷之氣如牛羊群畜穹閭，南夷之氣類舟船幡旗。

translations.literal: In general, sea-shore mirage-qi like towers and terraces; broad-field qi forming palaces and gate-towers; northern barbarian qi like cattle and sheep in herds and yurts; southern barbarian qi like boats, ships, banners, and flags.
translations.idiomatic: Coastal mirages like towers, open-country vapor like palaces, northern barbarian vapor like herds and yurts, southern barbarian vapor like ships and banners.

sentences.zh: 自華以南，氣下黑上赤。

translations.literal: From Hua southward, qi is black below and red above.
translations.idiomatic: South of Mount Hua, vapor is black below and red above.

sentences.zh: 嵩高、三河之郊，氣正赤。

translations.literal: At Songgao and the suburbs of the Three Rivers, qi is pure red.
translations.idiomatic: At Mount Song and the Three Rivers region, vapor is pure red.

sentences.zh: 恆山之北，氣青。

translations.literal: North of Mount Heng, qi is green.
translations.idiomatic: North of Mount Heng, vapor is green.

sentences.zh: 勃、碣、海、岱之間，氣皆正黑。

translations.literal: Between Bo, Jie, the sea, and Mount Dai, qi is all pure black.
translations.idiomatic: Between Bo, Jie, the coast, and Mount Tai, vapor is pure black.

sentences.zh: 江湖之間，氣皆白。

translations.literal: Between rivers and lakes, qi is all white.
translations.idiomatic: Between the great rivers and lakes, vapor is white.

sentences.zh: 東海氣如圓簦。

translations.literal: Eastern sea qi is like a round bamboo hat.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern sea vapor resembles a round bamboo hat.

sentences.zh: 附漢、河水，氣如引布。

translations.literal: Fuhan and the Yellow River—qi like drawn silk.
translations.idiomatic: At Fuhan and the Yellow River, vapor is like drawn silk.

sentences.zh: 江、漢氣勁如杼。

translations.literal: Yangtze and Han—qi vigorous like a loom shuttle.
translations.idiomatic: Along the Yangtze and Han, vapor is vigorous like a shuttle.

sentences.zh: 濟水氣如黑㹠。

translations.literal: Ji River qi is like a black pig.
translations.idiomatic: Ji River vapor resembles a black pig.

sentences.zh: 滑水氣如狼白尾。

translations.literal: Hua River qi is like a wolf with white tail.
translations.idiomatic: Hua River vapor looks like a wolf with a white tail.

sentences.zh: 淮南氣如帛。

translations.literal: Huai River qi is like silk.
translations.idiomatic: Huai River vapor is like silk.

sentences.zh: 少室氣如白兔青尾。

translations.literal: Shaoshi qi is like a white rabbit with green tail.
translations.idiomatic: Mount Shaoshi vapor resembles a white rabbit with a green tail.

sentences.zh: 恆山氣如黑牛青尾。

translations.literal: Mount Heng qi is like a black ox with green tail.
translations.idiomatic: Mount Heng vapor looks like a black ox with a green tail.

sentences.zh: 東夷氣如樹，西夷氣如室屋，南夷氣如闍台，或類舟船。

translations.literal: Eastern barbarian qi is like trees; western barbarian qi like houses; southern barbarian qi like tower-gates, or like boats and ships.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern barbarian vapor is tree-like; western, house-like; southern, tower- or ship-like.

sentences.zh: 陣雲如立垣，杼軸雲類軸搏，兩端銳。

translations.literal: Battle-line clouds like standing walls; spindle clouds like axle hubs, sharp at both ends.
translations.idiomatic: Battle-line clouds stand like walls; spindle clouds like axle hubs, sharp at both ends.

sentences.zh: 㣿雲如繩，居前亙天，其半半天，其蛪者類闕旗，故鉤雲勾曲。

translations.literal: Hooked clouds like ropes, advancing and spanning heaven—half spans half the sky; the curved sort resembles gate flags—hence hooked clouds are bent and curved.
translations.idiomatic: Rope-like hooked clouds span heaven—half the sky at a time; their curves resemble gate banners.

sentences.zh: 諸此雲見，以五色占而澤摶密。

translations.literal: When all these clouds appear, read them by five colors and by moistness, density, and mass.
translations.idiomatic: When these clouds appear, judge them by color, moisture, and density.

sentences.zh: 其見，動人及有兵，必起合鬭。

translations.literal: When they appear, if they stir people and there are armies, warfare is certain to rise and armies will clash.
translations.idiomatic: When they appear with armies abroad, war and battle are certain.

sentences.zh: 其直，雲氣如三匹帛，廣前銳後，大軍行氣也。

translations.literal: The straight sort—cloud-qi like three bolts of silk, broad in front and sharp behind—qi of a great army on the march.
translations.idiomatic: Straight cloud-vapor like three bolts of silk, broad in front and sharp behind, marks a great army marching.

sentences.zh: 韓雲如布，趙雲如牛，楚雲如日，宋雲如車，魯雲如馬，衛雲如犬，周雲如車輪，秦雲如行人，魏雲如鼠，鄭、齊雲如絳衣，越雲如龍，蜀雲如囷。

translations.literal: Han clouds like cloth, Zhao clouds like oxen, Chu clouds like the sun, Song clouds like chariots, Lu clouds like horses, Wei clouds like dogs, Zhou clouds like chariot wheels, Qin clouds like travelers, Wei clouds like rats, Zheng and Qi clouds like crimson robes, Yue clouds like dragons, Shu clouds like granaries.
translations.idiomatic: Han vapor is cloth-like, Zhao ox-like, Chu sun-like, Song chariot-like, Lu horse-like, Wei dog-like, Zhou wheel-like, Qin traveler-like, Wei rat-like, Zheng and Qi crimson-robed, Yue dragon-like, Shu granary-like.

sentences.zh: 車氣乍高乍下，往往而聚。

translations.literal: Chariot qi now high now low, often gathering.
translations.idiomatic: Chariot vapor rises and falls, often clustering.

sentences.zh: 騎氣卑而布，卒氣摶。

translations.literal: Cavalry qi is low and spread; infantry qi is massed.
translations.idiomatic: Cavalry vapor lies low and spread; infantry vapor is tightly massed.

sentences.zh: 前卑後高者疾，前方而高，後銳而卑者卻。

translations.literal: Low in front and high behind means swift; square in front and high, sharp behind and low means retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Low front and high back means speed; square high front and sharp low rear means retreat.

sentences.zh: 其氣平者，其行徐。

translations.literal: When its qi is level, its movement is slow.
translations.idiomatic: Level vapor means slow movement.

sentences.zh: 前高後卑者，不止而返。

translations.literal: High in front and low behind—does not advance but returns.
translations.idiomatic: High front and low back means no advance—only return.

sentences.zh: 校騎之氣正蒼黑，長數百丈，遊兵之氣如彗掃，一云長數百丈，無根本。

translations.literal: Scout-cavalry qi is pure dark green, several hundred zhang long; roaming-army qi is like a comet sweeping—some say several hundred zhang, without root or base.
translations.idiomatic: Scout vapor is dark green, hundreds of zhang long; roaming-army vapor sweeps like a comet, hundreds of zhang without root.

sentences.zh: 喜氣上黃下白，怒氣上下赤，憂氣上下黑，土功氣黃白，徙氣白。

translations.literal: Joy-qi is yellow above and white below; anger-qi red above and below; sorrow-qi black above and below; earthworks-qi yellow-white; migration-qi white.
translations.idiomatic: Joy-vapor is yellow above, white below; anger, red throughout; sorrow, black throughout; earthworks, yellow-white; migration, white.

sentences.zh: 凡候氣之法，氣初出時，若雲非雲，若霧非霧，仿佛若可見。

translations.literal: In general, the method of observing qi: when qi first issues, like cloud yet not cloud, like fog yet not fog, dimly as if visible.
translations.idiomatic: To observe qi: when it first rises, neither quite cloud nor fog, barely visible.

sentences.zh: 初出森森然，在桑榆上，高五六尺者，是千五百里外。

translations.literal: When first issuing, dense and thick, on mulberry and elm trees, five or six chi high—this is fifteen hundred li away.
translations.idiomatic: Dense vapor first appearing on mulberry and elm trees five or six chi high marks an army fifteen hundred li away.

sentences.zh: 平視則千里，舉目望則五百里。

translations.literal: Viewed level, a thousand li; looking up, five hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: At eye level, a thousand li; looking upward, five hundred li.

sentences.zh: 仰瞻中天，則百里內。

translations.literal: Looking up at mid-heaven—a hundred li within.
translations.idiomatic: Vapor at mid-heaven means within a hundred li.

sentences.zh: 平望桑榆間二千里，登高而望，下屬地者，三千里。

translations.literal: Level view between mulberry and elm—two thousand li; climbing high to look, reaching down to earth—three thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Level sight between mulberry and elm marks two thousand li; from a height reaching to earth, three thousand li.

sentences.zh: 凡欲知我軍氣，常以甲巳日及庚、子、辰、戌、午、未、亥日，及八月十八日，去軍十里許，登高望之可見，依別記占之。

translations.literal: In general, to know our army's qi, regularly on jiaji days and geng, zi, chen, xu, wu, wei, and hai days, and on the eighteenth day of the eighth month, go ten li from the army, climb high and look—it can be seen; read it according to separate records.
translations.idiomatic: To read our army's vapor, on jia/ji days and geng, zi, chen, xu, wu, wei, hai days—and the eighteenth of the eighth month—climb a height ten li from camp and judge by the manuals.

sentences.zh: 百人以上皆有氣。

translations.literal: A force of a hundred men or more all has qi.
translations.idiomatic: Any force of a hundred men or more gives off vapor.

sentences.zh: 凡占災異，先推九宮分野，六壬日月，不應陰霧風雨而陰霧者，乃可占。

translations.literal: In general, when divining calamities and anomalies, first calculate the Nine Palaces and territorial divisions, and the six ren days and months; when yin, fog, wind, and rain should not appear yet fog appears—only then may one divin.
translations.idiomatic: To read calamities, first calculate the Nine Palaces, territorial divisions, and six ren cycles; only when fog appears contrary to weather may one interpret omens.

sentences.zh: 對敵而坐，氣來甚卑下，其陰覆人，上掩溝蓋道者，是大賊必至。

translations.literal: Sitting facing the enemy, qi coming very low, its yin covering men, above masking ditches and roads—great bandits are certain to arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Facing the enemy, vapor coming very low and covering men and roads means great raiders are near.

sentences.zh: 敵在東，日出候。

translations.literal: Enemy in the east—observe at sunrise.
translations.idiomatic: Enemy to the east: observe at sunrise.

sentences.zh: 在南，日中候。

translations.literal: In the south—observe at midday.
translations.idiomatic: Enemy to the south: observe at noon.

sentences.zh: 在西，日入候。

translations.literal: In the west—observe at sunset.
translations.idiomatic: Enemy to the west: observe at sunset.

sentences.zh: 在北，夜半候。

translations.literal: In the north—observe at midnight.
translations.idiomatic: Enemy to the north: observe at midnight.

sentences.zh: 王相色吉，囚死色凶。

translations.literal: Wang and xiang colors are auspicious; imprisoned and dead colors are inauspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Prosperous colors are lucky; imprisoned and dead colors, ill.

sentences.zh: 凡軍上氣，高勝下，厚勝薄，實勝虛，長勝短，澤勝枯。

translations.literal: In general, army upper qi—high defeats low, thick defeats thin, solid defeats hollow, long defeats short, moist defeats dry.
translations.idiomatic: Army vapor: high beats low, thick beats thin, solid beats hollow, long beats short, moist beats dry.

sentences.zh: 我軍在西，賊軍在東，氣西厚東薄，西長東短，西高東下，凱撒東枯，則知我軍必勝。

translations.literal: Our army in the west, bandit army in the east—qi thick in the west and thin in the east, long in the west and short in the east, high in the west and low in the east, moist in the west and dry in the east—then know our army is certain to win.
translations.idiomatic: Our force west, enemy east: thicker, longer, higher, moister vapor in the west means we will win.

sentences.zh: 凡氣初出，似甑上氣，勃勃上升。

translations.literal: In general, when qi first issues, it is like qi on a steamer, surging upward vigorously.
translations.idiomatic: Fresh vapor rises like steam from a cauldron, surging upward.

sentences.zh: 氣積為霧，霧為陰，陰氣結為虹蜺姿暈珥之屬。

translations.literal: Qi accumulating becomes fog; fog is yin; yin qi coalescing becomes rainbows, secondary rainbows, halos, ear-pendants, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: Accumulated vapor becomes fog; fog is yin; yin coalescing forms rainbows, halos, ear-pendants, and the like.

sentences.zh: 凡氣不積不結，散漫一方，不能為災。

translations.literal: In general, qi that does not accumulate and coalesce, scattered over one region, cannot become disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Vapor that never gathers and coalesces, scattered in one quarter, cannot bring disaster.

sentences.zh: 必須和雜殺氣，森森然疾起，乃可論占。

translations.literal: It must mix with killing-qi, rising densely and swiftly—only then may one discuss and interpret.
translations.idiomatic: It must mingle with killing vapor, rising dense and swift—only then may one interpret omens.

sentences.zh: 軍上氣安則軍安，氣不安則軍不安。

translations.literal: When army upper qi is calm, the army is calm; when qi is unsettled, the army is unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: Calm army vapor means a calm host; restless vapor, a restless host.

sentences.zh: 氣南北則軍南北，氣東西則軍亦東西。

translations.literal: Qi to south and north, the army to south and north; qi to east and west, the army likewise east and west.
translations.idiomatic: Vapor to north and south means the army moves north and south; vapor east and west, the army moves likewise.

sentences.zh: 氣散則為軍破敗。

translations.literal: When qi disperses, the army is broken and defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Dispersed vapor means a broken, defeated army.

sentences.zh: 候氣，常以平旦、下晡、日出沒時處氣，以見知大。

translations.literal: Observing qi, regularly at daybreak, late afternoon, and at sunrise and sunset—judge the great from what is seen.
translations.idiomatic: Observe vapor at dawn, late afternoon, and sunrise or sunset to read the larger omen.

sentences.zh: 占期內有大風雨久陰，則災不成。

translations.literal: Within the period of interpretation, if there is great wind, rain, or long overcast, the disaster does not come to pass.
translations.idiomatic: If great wind, rain, or prolonged cloud cover falls within the predicted period, the disaster fails to materialize.

sentences.zh: 故風以散之，陰以諫之，雲以幡之，雨以厭之。

translations.literal: Therefore wind disperses it, overcast remonstrates against it, clouds banner it, rain suppresses it.
translations.idiomatic: Wind disperses the omen, overcast warns against it, clouds signal it, and rain quells it.

sentences.zh: 五代災變應梁武帝天監元年八月壬寅，熒惑守南斗。

translations.literal: Calamities and anomalies of the Five Dynasties period, corresponding to the first year of Emperor Wu of Liang's Tianjian reign, eighth month, renyin day—Mars guarding the Southern Dipper.
translations.idiomatic: Calamities matching the omen of Mars in the Southern Dipper on renyin day, eighth month, first year of Liang Wudi's Tianjian reign:

sentences.zh: 占曰：「糴貴，五穀不成，大旱，多火災，吳、越有憂，宰相死。

translations.literal: Interpretation says: "Grain is dear, the five grains do not ripen, great drought, many fires; Wu and Yue have sorrow; the chief minister dies."
translations.idiomatic: The reading says: "Grain grows costly, crops fail, drought and fire multiply; Wu and Yue face grief; the chief minister dies."

sentences.zh: 」是歲大旱，米鬭五千，人多餓死。

translations.literal: That year there was great drought; rice was five thousand per dou; many people starved to death.
translations.idiomatic: That year brought severe drought; rice cost five thousand cash per dou and many starved.

sentences.zh: 其二年五月，尚書范雲卒。

translations.literal: In the second year, fifth month, Minister of the Secretariat Fan Yun died.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, fifth month, Fan Yun, Minister of the Secretariat, died.

sentences.zh: 二年五月丙辰，月犯心。

translations.literal: Second year, fifth month, bingchen day—the moon violated the Heart.
translations.idiomatic: Second year, fifth month, bingchen: the moon crossed the Heart constellation.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「有亂臣，不出三年，有亡國。

translations.literal: Interpretation says: "There is a rebellious minister; within three years, a state perishes."
translations.idiomatic: The reading says: "A rebellious minister appears; within three years a state falls."

sentences.zh: 」其四年，交州刺史李凱舉兵反。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Inspector of Jiaozhou Li Kai raised troops in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, Li Kai, Inspector of Jiaozhou, rebelled with an army.

sentences.zh: 七月丙子，太白犯軒轅大星。

translations.literal: Seventh month, bingzi day—Venus violated the great star of the Chariot.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh month, bingzi: Venus crossed the Chariot's great star.

sentences.zh: 四年六月壬戌，歲星晝見。

translations.literal: Fourth year, sixth month, renxu day—Jupiter was visible by day.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth year, sixth month, renxu: Jupiter appeared in daylight.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「歲色黃潤，立竿影見，大熟。

translations.literal: Interpretation says: "Jupiter's color yellow and moist, standing pole shadow visible—great ripening."
translations.idiomatic: The reading says: "Yellow, moist Jupiter with visible pole shadow means a great harvest."

sentences.zh: 」是歲大穰，米斛三十。

translations.literal: That year there was great abundance; rice was thirty per hu.
translations.idiomatic: That year brought great abundance; rice cost thirty cash per hu.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「星與日爭光，武且弱，文且強。

translations.literal: It is also said: "The star contends in light with the sun—military power weakens, civil power strengthens."
translations.idiomatic: It also says: "When a star rivals the sun in brightness, military power weakens and civil power grows."

sentences.zh: 」自此後，帝崇尚文儒，躬自講說，終於太清，不修武備。

translations.literal: From this time onward, the Emperor honored literary Confucianism, personally lecturing, until the Taiping era without repairing military preparations.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the emperor favored letters and Confucian learning, lecturing in person, and until the Taiping era neglected military readiness.

sentences.zh: 八月庚子，老人星見。

translations.literal: Eighth month, gengzi day—the Old Man star appeared.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth month, gengzi: the Old Man star appeared.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「老人星見，人主壽昌。

translations.literal: Interpretation says: "When the Old Man star appears, the ruler enjoys long life and prosperity."
translations.idiomatic: The reading says: "The Old Man star's appearance brings the ruler long life and prosperity."

sentences.zh: 」自此後，每年恆以秋分後見於參南，至春分而伏。

translations.literal: From this time onward, every year after the autumn equinox it appeared south of Shen, hiding at the spring equinox.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter it appeared south of Shen after each autumn equinox and vanished at the spring equinox.

sentences.zh: 武帝壽考之象云。

translations.literal: An image of Emperor Wu's long life.
translations.idiomatic: A sign of Emperor Wu's longevity.

sentences.zh: 七年九月巳亥，月犯東井。

translations.literal: Seventh year, ninth month, jihai day—the moon violated the Eastern Well.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh year, ninth month, jihai: the moon crossed the Eastern Well.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「有水災。

translations.literal: Interpretation says: "There is flood disaster."
translations.idiomatic: The reading says: "Flood disaster follows."

sentences.zh: 」其年京師大水。

translations.literal: That year the capital region suffered great flood.
translations.idiomatic: That year the capital region flooded severely.

sentences.zh: 十年九月丙申，天西北隆隆有聲，赤氣上至地。

translations.literal: Tenth year, ninth month, bingshen day—in the northwest of heaven a rumbling sound, red qi reaching to earth.
translations.idiomatic: Tenth year, ninth month, bingshen: thunder rolled in the northwest and red vapor reached the ground.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「天狗也，所往之鄉有流血，其君失地。

translations.literal: Interpretation says: "The Heavenly Dog; where it goes there is flowing blood; its ruler loses territory."
translations.idiomatic: The reading says: "The Heavenly Dog; blood flows where it passes; the ruler loses land."

sentences.zh: 」其年十二月，馬仙琕大敗魏軍，斬馘十余萬，克復朐山城。

translations.literal: That year, twelfth month, Ma Xianbi greatly defeated the Wei army, beheading over a hundred thousand, and recovered Mount Xiongshan city.
translations.idiomatic: That year, twelfth month, Ma Xianbi crushed the Wei army, beheading over a hundred thousand and retaking Xiongshan.

sentences.zh: 十二月壬戌朔，日食，在牛四度。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, renxu new moon—solar eclipse, in Ox four degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Twelfth month, renxu new moon: solar eclipse at four degrees of the Ox.

sentences.zh: 十三年二月丙午，太白失行，在天關。

translations.literal: Thirteenth year, second month, bingwu day—Venus lost its proper motion, at the Celestial Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Thirteenth year, second month, bingwu: Venus strayed from its course at the Celestial Gate.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「津梁不通，又兵起。

translations.literal: Interpretation says: "Fords and bridges are blocked; moreover armies rise."
translations.idiomatic: The reading says: "Crossings and bridges are blocked; armies also rise."

sentences.zh: 」其年填星守天江。

translations.literal: That year Saturn guarded the Celestial River.
translations.idiomatic: That year Saturn stood in the Celestial River.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「有江河塞，有決溢，有土功。

translations.literal: Interpretation says: "Rivers are blocked, there are breaches and overflows, there are earthworks."
translations.idiomatic: The reading says: "Rivers clog, burst, and overflow; public earthworks follow."

sentences.zh: 」其年，大發軍眾造浮山堰，以堨淮水。

translations.literal: That year, great numbers of troops were mobilized to build the Floating Mountain weir, damming the Huai River.
translations.idiomatic: That year vast forces built the Floating Mountain weir to dam the Huai.

sentences.zh: 至十四年，填星移去天江而堰壞，奔流決溢。

translations.literal: By the fourteenth year, Saturn moved away from the Celestial River and the weir collapsed, rushing and overflowing in breach.
translations.idiomatic: By the fourteenth year Saturn left the Celestial River, the weir collapsed, and the waters burst forth.

sentences.zh: 十四年十月辛未，太白犯南斗。

translations.literal: Fourteenth year, tenth month, xinwei day—Venus violated the Southern Dipper.
translations.idiomatic: Fourteenth year, tenth month, xinwei: Venus crossed the Southern Dipper.

sentences.zh: 十七年閏八月戊辰，月行掩昴。

translations.literal: Seventeenth year, intercalary eighth month, wuchen day—the moon moved, masking the Pleiades.
translations.idiomatic: Seventeenth year, intercalary eighth month, wuchen: the moon occulted the Pleiades.

sentences.zh: 普通元年春正月丙子，日有食之。

translations.literal: Putong first year, spring, first month, bingzi day—there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: Putong first year, spring, first month, bingzi: solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「日食，陰侵陽，陽不克陰也。

translations.literal: Interpretation says: "Solar eclipse—yin invades yang; yang cannot overcome yin."
translations.idiomatic: The reading says: "Solar eclipse: yin invades yang; yang cannot overcome yin."

sentences.zh: 為大水。

translations.literal: There will be great flood.
translations.idiomatic: Great floods follow.

sentences.zh: 」其年七月，江、淮、海溢。

translations.literal: That year, seventh month, the Yangtze, Huai, and sea overflowed.
translations.idiomatic: That year, seventh month, the Yangtze, Huai, and sea flooded.

sentences.zh: 九月乙亥，有星晨見東方，光爛如火。

translations.literal: Ninth month, yihai day—a star appeared at dawn in the east, its light blazing like fire.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth month, yihai: a star appeared at dawn in the east, blazing like fire.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「國皇見，有內難，有急兵反叛。

translations.literal: Interpretation says: "The National Sovereign star appears; there is internal trouble; there are urgent armies in rebellion."
translations.idiomatic: The reading says: "The National Sovereign star appears: internal turmoil and urgent rebellion follow."

sentences.zh: 」其三年，義州刺史文僧朗以州叛。

translations.literal: In the third year, Inspector of Yizhou Wen Senglang rebelled with his province.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, Wen Senglang, Inspector of Yizhou, rebelled with his province.

sentences.zh: 四年十一月癸未朔，日有食之，太白晝見。

translations.literal: Fourth year, eleventh month, guiwei new moon—solar eclipse; Venus visible by day.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth year, eleventh month, guiwei new moon: solar eclipse; Venus visible by day.

sentences.zh: 六年三月丙午，歲星入南斗。

translations.literal: Sixth year, third month, bingwu day—Jupiter entered the Southern Dipper.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth year, third month, bingwu: Jupiter entered the Southern Dipper.

sentences.zh: 庚申，月食。

translations.literal: Gengshen day—lunar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: Gengshen: lunar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 五月己酉，太白晝見。

translations.literal: Fifth month, jiyou day—Venus visible by day.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth month, jiyou: Venus visible by day.

sentences.zh: 六月癸未，太白經天。

translations.literal: Sixth month, guiwei day—Venus crossed the sky.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth month, guiwei: Venus crossed the meridian by day.

sentences.zh: 九月壬子，太白犯右執法。

translations.literal: Ninth month, renzi day—Venus violated the Right Law-enforcer.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth month, renzi: Venus crossed the Right Law-enforcer.

sentences.zh: 七年正月癸卯，太白歲星在牛相犯。

translations.literal: Seventh year, first month, guimao day—Venus and Jupiter in the Ox mutually violated each other.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh year, first month, guimao: Venus and Jupiter clashed in the Ox.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「其國君凶，易政。

translations.literal: Interpretation says: "That state's ruler is ill-fated; government changes."
translations.idiomatic: The reading says: "The ruler is doomed; the regime changes."

sentences.zh: 」明年三月，改元，大赦。

translations.literal: The next year, third month, the era name was changed and a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, third month, the era name changed and a general amnesty followed.

sentences.zh: 大通元年八月甲申，月掩填星。

translations.literal: Datong first year, eighth month, jiashen day—the moon masked Saturn.
translations.idiomatic: Datong first year, eighth month, jiashen: the moon occulted Saturn.

sentences.zh: 閏月癸酉，又掩之。

translations.literal: Intercalary month, guiyou day—it masked Saturn again.
translations.idiomatic: Intercalary month, guiyou: it occulted Saturn again.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「有大喪，天下無主，國易政。

translations.literal: Interpretation says: "There is great mourning; the realm has no lord; the state changes government."
translations.idiomatic: The reading says: "Great mourning follows; the realm lacks a ruler; government changes."

sentences.zh: 」其後中大通元年九月癸巳，上又幸同泰寺捨身，王公以一億萬錢奉贖。

translations.literal: Afterward, in Zhongdatong first year, ninth month, guisi day, the Emperor again visited Tongtai Temple to renounce the throne, and princes and nobles paid a hundred million cash for his ransom.
translations.idiomatic: Later, Zhongdatong first year, ninth month, guisi, the emperor again "abdicated" at Tongtai Temple; princes paid a hundred million cash to ransom him.

sentences.zh: 十月己酉還宮，大赦，改元。

translations.literal: Tenth month, jiyou day he returned to the palace, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the era name.
translations.idiomatic: Tenth month, jiyou, he returned to the palace, amnestied the realm, and changed the era name.

sentences.zh: 中大通三年，太子薨，皆天下無主、易政及大喪之應。

translations.literal: Zhongdatong third year, the Crown Prince died—all responses to the realm having no lord, change of government, and great mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongdatong third year the crown prince died—fulfilling the omens of a lordless realm, regime change, and great mourning.

sentences.zh: 中大通元年閏月壬戌，熒惑犯鬼積屍。

translations.literal: Zhongdatong first year, intercalary month, renxu day—Mars violated the Ghost Heap of Corpses.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongdatong first year, intercalary month, renxu: Mars crossed the Ghost Heap of Corpses.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「有大喪，有大兵，破軍殺將。

translations.literal: Interpretation says: "There is great mourning; there is great warfare; armies are broken and generals killed."
translations.idiomatic: The reading says: "Great mourning, great war, shattered armies, and slain generals follow."

sentences.zh: 」其二年，蕭玩帥眾援巴州，為魏梁州軍所敗，玩被殺。

translations.literal: In the second year, Xiao Wan led troops to aid Bazhou and was defeated by the Wei army of Liang Province; Wan was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Second year, Xiao Wan led troops to relieve Bazhou, was beaten by Wei forces of Liang Province, and was killed.

sentences.zh: 四年七月甲辰，星隕如雨。

translations.literal: Fourth year, seventh month, jiachen day—stars fell like rain.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth year, seventh month, jiachen: stars fell like rain.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「星隕，陽失其位，災害之象萌也。

translations.literal: Interpretation says: "Stars falling—yang loses its place; the image of disaster sprouts."
translations.idiomatic: The reading says: "Falling stars mean yang loses its place—the first sprouting of disaster."

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「星隕如雨，人民叛，下有專討。

translations.literal: It is also said: "Stars falling like rain—the people rebel; below there is a special punitive campaign."
translations.idiomatic: It also says: "Stars falling like rain: the people rebel and punitive campaigns follow."

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「大人憂。

translations.literal: It is also said: "The great man grieves."
translations.idiomatic: It also says: "The great man grieves."

sentences.zh: 」其後侯景狡亂，帝以憂崩，人眾奔散，皆其應也。

translations.literal: Afterward Hou Jing's treacherous rebellion, the Emperor died of grief, and the multitude scattered—all these were the responses.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Hou Jing's rebellion, the emperor died of grief, and the people scattered—all as foretold.

sentences.zh: 五年正月己酉，長星見。

translations.literal: Fifth year, first month, jiyou day—a long-tailed star appeared.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth year, first month, jiyou: a long-tailed star appeared.

sentences.zh: 六年四月丁卯，熒惑在南斗。

translations.literal: Sixth year, fourth month, dingmao day—Mars was in the Southern Dipper.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth year, fourth month, dingmao: Mars stood in the Southern Dipper.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「熒惑出入留舍南斗中，有賊臣謀反，天下易政，更元。

translations.literal: Interpretation says: "Mars entering, leaving, or dwelling in the Southern Dipper—there is a treacherous minister in rebellion; the realm changes government and the era name."
translations.idiomatic: The reading says: "Mars entering, leaving, or dwelling in the Southern Dipper: a treacherous minister rebels; the realm changes rulers and era names."

sentences.zh: 」其年十二月，北梁州刺史蘭欽舉兵反，後年改為大同元年。

translations.literal: That year, twelfth month, Inspector of Northern Liangzhou Lan Qin raised troops in rebellion; the next year the era was changed to Datong first year.
translations.idiomatic: That year, twelfth month, Lan Qin, Inspector of Northern Liangzhou, rebelled; the next year the era became Datong.

sentences.zh: 大同三年三月乙丑，歲星掩建星。

translations.literal: Datong third year, third month, yichou day—Jupiter masked the Establishment star.
translations.idiomatic: Datong third year, third month, yichou: Jupiter occulted the Establishment star.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「有反臣。

translations.literal: Interpretation says: "There is a rebellious minister."
translations.idiomatic: The reading says: "A rebellious minister appears."

sentences.zh: 」其年，會稽山賊起。

translations.literal: That year, bandits rose on Mount Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: That year bandits rose on Mount Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 其七年，交州刺史李賁舉兵反。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, Inspector of Jiaozhou Li Ben raised troops in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, Li Ben, Inspector of Jiaozhou, rebelled with an army.

sentences.zh: 五年十月辛丑，彗出南斗，長一尺余，東南指，漸長一丈餘。

translations.literal: Fifth year, tenth month, xinchou day—a comet issued from the Southern Dipper, one chi or more long, pointing southeast, gradually lengthening to more than one zhang.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth year, tenth month, xinchou: a comet issued from the Southern Dipper, over a chi long, pointing southeast, gradually stretching to more than a zhang.

sentences.zh: 十一月乙卯，至婁滅。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, yimao day—it reached Lou and vanished.
translations.idiomatic: Eleventh month, yimao: it reached Lou and disappeared.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「天下有謀王者。

translations.literal: Interpretation says: "Throughout the realm there is one who plots kingship."
translations.idiomatic: The reading says: "Someone in the realm plots to become king."

sentences.zh: 」其八年正月，安成民劉敬躬挾左道以反，党與數萬。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, first month, the people of Ancheng, Liu Jinggong, relied on heterodox ways to rebel, with followers numbering tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth year, first month, Liu Jinggong of Ancheng rebelled through heterodox cults with tens of thousands of followers.

sentences.zh: 其九年，李賁僭稱皇帝于交州。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, Li Ben arrogated the title of emperor in Jiaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth year, Li Ben declared himself emperor in Jiaozhou.

sentences.zh: 太清二年五月，兩月見。

translations.literal: Taiqing second year, fifth month—two moons appeared.
translations.idiomatic: Taiqing second year, fifth month: two moons appeared.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「其國亂，必見於亡國。

translations.literal: Interpretation says: "That state is in disorder; it is certain to appear at the fall of a state."
translations.idiomatic: The reading says: "The state falls into disorder; this omen appears as kingdoms collapse."

translations.literal: (Closing quotation.)
translations.idiomatic: (This closes the omen text cited above.)

sentences.zh: 三年正月壬午，熒惑守心。

translations.literal: Third year, first month, renwu day—Mars guarded the Heart.
translations.idiomatic: Third year, first month, renwu: Mars guarded the Heart.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「王者惡之。

translations.literal: Interpretation says: "Kings detest it."
translations.idiomatic: The reading says: "Kings dread this omen."

sentences.zh: 」乙酉，太白晝見。

translations.literal: Yiyou day—Venus visible by day.
translations.idiomatic: Yiyou: Venus visible by day.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「不出三年，有大喪，天下革政更王，強國弱，小國強。

translations.literal: Interpretation says: "Within three years, great mourning; the realm changes government and kings; strong states weaken, small states strengthen."
translations.idiomatic: The reading says: "Within three years: great mourning, regime change, strong states weaken and small states grow strong."

sentences.zh: 」三月丙子，熒惑又守心。

translations.literal: Third month, bingzi day—Mars again guarded the Heart.
translations.idiomatic: Third month, bingzi: Mars again guarded the Heart.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「大人易政，主去其宮。

translations.literal: Interpretation says: "The great man changes government; the ruler leaves his palace."
translations.idiomatic: The reading says: "The sovereign changes regime; the ruler leaves his palace."

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「人饑亡，海內哭，天下大潰。

translations.literal: It is also said: "People starve and perish; the realm weeps; the realm collapses greatly."
translations.idiomatic: It also says: "People starve; the realm weeps; the empire collapses."

sentences.zh: 」是年，帝為侯景所幽，崩。

translations.literal: That year, the Emperor was imprisoned by Hou Jing and died.
translations.idiomatic: That year the emperor was imprisoned by Hou Jing and died.

sentences.zh: 七月，九江大饑，人相食十四五。

translations.literal: Seventh month, Jiujiang suffered great famine; people ate one another, fourteen or fifteen out of ten.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh month, Jiujiang suffered famine so severe that fourteen or fifteen people in ten resorted to cannibalism.

sentences.zh: 九月戊午，月在斗，掩歲星。

translations.literal: Ninth month, wuwu day—the moon was in the Dipper, masking Jupiter.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth month, wuwu: the moon in the Dipper occulted Jupiter.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「天下亡君。

translations.literal: Interpretation says: "The realm loses its ruler."
translations.idiomatic: The reading says: "The realm loses its ruler."

sentences.zh: 」其後侯景篡殺。

translations.literal: Afterward Hou Jing usurped and killed.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Hou Jing usurped power and murdered the emperor.

sentences.zh: 簡文帝大寶元年正月丙寅，月晝光見。

translations.literal: Emperor Jianwen, Dabao first year, first month, bingyin day—the moon's light was visible by day.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jianwen, Dabao first year, first month, bingyin: the moon was visible by day.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「月晝光，有隱謀，國雄逃。

translations.literal: Interpretation says: "Moonlight by day—there is hidden plotting; the state's strength flees."
translations.idiomatic: The reading says: "Daylight moon: hidden plots; the state's power flees."

sentences.zh: 」又云：「月晝明，奸邪並作，擅君之朝。

translations.literal: It is also said: "The moon bright by day—evil men act together, usurping the ruler's court."
translations.idiomatic: It also says: "A bright moon by day: villains seize the court."

sentences.zh: 」其後侯景篡殺，皆國亂亡君。

translations.literal: Afterward Hou Jing usurped and killed—all disorder of the state and loss of ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Hou Jing usurped and killed—all the chaos of a fallen state.

sentences.zh: 大喪更政之應也。

translations.literal: Responses to great mourning and change of government.
translations.idiomatic: Fulfillments of great mourning and regime change.

sentences.zh: 元帝承聖三年九月甲午，月犯心中星。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan, Chengsheng third year, ninth month, jiawu day—the moon violated the central star of the Heart.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan, Chengsheng third year, ninth month, jiawu: the moon crossed the Heart's central star.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「有反臣，王者惡之，有亡國。

translations.literal: Interpretation says: "There is a rebellious minister; kings detest it; there is loss of a state."
translations.idiomatic: The reading says: "A rebellious minister appears; kings dread it; a state falls."

sentences.zh: 」其後三年，帝為周軍所俘執，陳氏取國，梁氏以亡。

translations.literal: Afterward, within three years, the Emperor was captured and held by the Zhou army; the Chen clan took the realm and the Liang house perished.
translations.idiomatic: Within three years the emperor was captured by Zhou forces, Chen seized the realm, and the Liang dynasty ended.

sentences.zh: 陳武帝永定三年九月辛卯朔，月入南斗。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Chen, Yongding third year, ninth month, xinmao new moon—the moon entered the Southern Dipper.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Wudi, Yongding third year, ninth month, xinmao new moon: the moon entered the Southern Dipper.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「月入南斗，大人憂。

translations.literal: Interpretation says: "When the moon enters the Southern Dipper, the great man grieves."
translations.idiomatic: The reading says: "The moon in the Southern Dipper brings grief to the great man."

sentences.zh: 」一曰：「太子殃。

translations.literal: One account says: "The crown prince suffers calamity."
translations.idiomatic: Another account says: "The crown prince faces disaster."

sentences.zh: 」後二年，帝崩，太子昌在周為質，文帝立。

translations.literal: Two years later the Emperor died; Crown Prince Chang was a hostage in Zhou; Emperor Wen was enthroned.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later the emperor died; Crown Prince Chang remained a Zhou hostage while Emperor Wen took the throne.

sentences.zh: 後昌還國，為侯安都遣盜迎殺之。

translations.literal: Afterward Chang returned to the realm and was murdered by bandits sent by Hou Andu to meet him.
translations.idiomatic: When Chang returned, Hou Andu sent assassins to kill him on the road.

sentences.zh: 三年五月丙辰朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: Third year, fifth month, bingchen new moon—solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: Third year, fifth month, bingchen new moon: solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「日食君傷。

translations.literal: Interpretation says: "Solar eclipse—the ruler is harmed."
translations.idiomatic: The reading says: "Solar eclipse: the ruler is harmed."

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「日食帝德消。

translations.literal: It is also said: "Solar eclipse—the emperor's virtue fades."
translations.idiomatic: It also says: "Solar eclipse: imperial virtue wanes."

sentences.zh: 」六月庚子，填星鉞與太白並。

translations.literal: Sixth month, gengzi day—Saturn's Halberd and Venus together.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth month, gengzi: Saturn's Halberd and Venus conjoined.

sentences.zh: 占：「太白與填合，為疾為內兵。

translations.literal: Interpretation: "Venus and Saturn conjoined—disease and internal warfare."
translations.idiomatic: The reading: "Venus and Saturn conjoined mean plague and civil war."

translations.literal: (Closing quotation.)
translations.idiomatic: (This closes the omen text cited above.)

sentences.zh: 文帝天嘉元年五月辛亥，熒惑犯右執法。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen, Tiancheng first year, fifth month, xinhai day—Mars violated the Right Law-enforcer.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen, Tiancheng first year, fifth month, xinhai: Mars crossed the Right Law-enforcer.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「大臣有憂，執法者誅。

translations.literal: Interpretation says: "Great ministers have sorrow; law-enforcers are executed."
translations.idiomatic: The reading says: "Great ministers face sorrow; law-enforcers are put to death."

sentences.zh: 」後四年，司空侯安都賜死。

translations.literal: Four years later, Minister of Works Hou Andu was ordered to commit suicide.
translations.idiomatic: Four years later, Hou Andu, Minister of Works, was forced to kill himself.

sentences.zh: 九月癸丑，彗星長四尺，見芒，指西南。

translations.literal: Ninth month, guichou day—a comet four chi long appeared with a tail, pointing southwest.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth month, guichou: a four-chi comet with a tail appeared, pointing southwest.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「彗星見則敵國兵起，得本者勝。

translations.literal: Interpretation says: "When a comet appears, enemy states raise armies; whoever gains its origin wins."
translations.idiomatic: The reading says: "Comets bring enemy armies; the side where it rises wins."

sentences.zh: 」其年，周將獨孤盛領眾趣巴湘，侯瑱襲破之。

translations.literal: That year, Zhou general Dugu Sheng led troops toward Ba and Xiang; Hou Tian surprised and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: That year Zhou general Dugu Sheng marched on Ba and Xiang; Hou Tian ambushed and routed him.

sentences.zh: 二年五月己酉，歲星守南斗。

translations.literal: Second year, fifth month, jiyou day—Jupiter guarded the Southern Dipper.
translations.idiomatic: Second year, fifth month, jiyou: Jupiter guarded the Southern Dipper.

sentences.zh: 六月丙戌，熒惑犯東井。

translations.literal: Sixth month, bingxu day—Mars violated the Eastern Well.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth month, bingxu: Mars crossed the Eastern Well.

sentences.zh: 七月乙丑，熒惑入鬼中。

translations.literal: Seventh month, yichou day—Mars entered the Ghost.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh month, yichou: Mars entered the Ghost.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，熒惑犯斧質。

translations.literal: Wuchen day—Mars violated the Axe-sentence.
translations.idiomatic: Wuchen: Mars crossed the Axe-sentence star.

sentences.zh: 十月，熒惑行在太微右掖門內。

translations.literal: Tenth month—Mars moved within the Right Crotch Gate of the Supreme Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Tenth month: Mars moved inside the Supreme Palace's Right Crotch Gate.

sentences.zh: 三年閏二月己丑，熒惑逆行，犯上相。

translations.literal: Third year, intercalary second month, jichou day—Mars moved retrograde and violated the Upper Minister.
translations.idiomatic: Third year, intercalary second month, jichou: Mars retrograded and crossed the Upper Minister.

sentences.zh: 甲子，太白犯五車、填星。

translations.literal: Jiazi day—Venus violated the Five Chariots and Saturn.
translations.idiomatic: Jiazi: Venus crossed the Five Chariots and Saturn.

sentences.zh: 七月，太白犯輿鬼。

translations.literal: Seventh month—Venus violated the Chariot Ghost.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh month: Venus crossed the Chariot Ghost.

sentences.zh: 八月癸卯，月犯南斗。

translations.literal: Eighth month, guimao day—the moon violated the Southern Dipper.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth month, guimao: the moon crossed the Southern Dipper.

sentences.zh: 丙午，月犯牽牛。

translations.literal: Bingwu day—the moon violated the Lead Ox.
translations.idiomatic: Bingwu: the moon crossed the Lead Ox.

sentences.zh: 庚甲，太白入太微。

translations.literal: Gengjia day—Venus entered the Supreme Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Gengjia: Venus entered the Supreme Palace.

sentences.zh: 十一月丁丑，月犯畢左股。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, dingchou day—the moon violated the left thigh of Net.
translations.idiomatic: Eleventh month, dingchou: the moon crossed the left thigh of Net.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，熒惑犯歲星。

translations.literal: Xinsi day—Mars violated Jupiter.
translations.idiomatic: Xinsi: Mars crossed Jupiter.

sentences.zh: 戊子，月犯角。

translations.literal: Wuzi day—the moon violated Horn.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzi: the moon crossed Horn.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，月入氐。

translations.literal: Gengyin day—the moon entered Dipper.
translations.idiomatic: Gengyin: the moon entered Dipper.

sentences.zh: 四年六月癸丑，太白犯右執法。

translations.literal: Fourth year, sixth month, guichou day—Venus violated the Right Law-enforcer.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth year, sixth month, guichou: Venus crossed the Right Law-enforcer.

sentences.zh: 七月戊子，熒惑犯填星。

translations.literal: Seventh month, wuzi day—Mars violated Saturn.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh month, wuzi: Mars crossed Saturn.

sentences.zh: 八月甲午，熒惑犯軒轅大星。

translations.literal: Eighth month, jiawu day—Mars violated the great star of the Chariot.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth month, jiawu: Mars crossed the Chariot's great star.

sentences.zh: 丁未，太白犯房。

translations.literal: Dingwei day—Venus violated Room.
translations.idiomatic: Dingwei: Venus crossed Room.

sentences.zh: 九月戊寅，熒惑入太微，犯右執法。

translations.literal: Ninth month, wuyin day—Mars entered the Supreme Palace and violated the Right Law-enforcer.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth month, wuyin: Mars entered the Supreme Palace and crossed the Right Law-enforcer.

sentences.zh: 癸未，太白入南斗。

translations.literal: Guiwei day—Venus entered the Southern Dipper.
translations.idiomatic: Guiwei: Venus entered the Southern Dipper.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「太白入斗，天下大亂，將相謀反，國易政。

translations.literal: Interpretation says: "Venus entering the Dipper—great disorder throughout the realm, generals and ministers plot rebellion, the state changes government."
translations.idiomatic: The reading says: "Venus in the Dipper: realm-wide chaos, ministerial rebellion, regime change."

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「君死，不死則廢。

translations.literal: It is also said: "The ruler dies; if not death, then deposition."
translations.idiomatic: It also says: "The ruler dies—or if not, is deposed."

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「天下受爵祿。

translations.literal: It is also said: "The realm receives ranks and salaries."
translations.idiomatic: It also says: "The realm receives ranks and salaries."

sentences.zh: 」其後安成王為太傅，廢少帝而自立，改官受爵之應也。

translations.literal: Afterward the Prince of Ancheng became Grand Tutor, deposed the young emperor and enthroned himself—the response to changing offices and receiving ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Prince of Ancheng became Grand Tutor, deposed the young emperor, and took the throne—fulfilling the omen of new offices and ranks.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，熒惑犯左執法。

translations.literal: Xinmao day—Mars violated the Left Law-enforcer.
translations.idiomatic: Xinmao: Mars crossed the Left Law-enforcer.

sentences.zh: 十一月辛酉，熒惑犯右執法。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, xinyou day—Mars violated the Right Law-enforcer.
translations.idiomatic: Eleventh month, xinyou: Mars crossed the Right Law-enforcer.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，月犯畢左股。

translations.literal: Jiaxu day—the moon violated the left thigh of Net.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaxu: the moon crossed the left thigh of Net.

sentences.zh: 五年正月甲子，月犯畢大星奎。

translations.literal: Fifth year, first month, jiazi day—the moon violated the great star of Net and Kui.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth year, first month, jiazi: the moon crossed Net's great star and Kui.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，月犯星。

translations.literal: Dingmao day—the moon violated a star.
translations.idiomatic: Dingmao: the moon crossed a star.

sentences.zh: 四月庚子，太白歲星合在奎，金在南，木在北，相去二尺許。

translations.literal: Fourth month, gengzi day—Venus and Jupiter conjoined in Kui, metal south and wood north, about two chi apart.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth month, gengzi: Venus and Jupiter conjoined in Kui, metal south and wood north, about two chi apart.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，月入氐，又犯熒惑，太白歲星又合，在婁，相去一尺許。

translations.literal: Renchen day—the moon entered Dipper and again violated Mars; Venus and Jupiter again conjoined in Bond, about one chi apart.
translations.idiomatic: Renchen: the moon entered Dipper and crossed Mars again; Venus and Jupiter conjoined again in Bond, about one chi apart.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，月犯房上星。

translations.literal: Guimao day—the moon violated the upper star of Room.
translations.idiomatic: Guimao: the moon crossed the upper star of Room.

sentences.zh: 五月庚午，熒惑逆行二十一日，犯氐東南、西南星。

translations.literal: Fifth month, gengwu day—Mars moved retrograde twenty-one days, violating southeast and southwest stars of Dipper.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth month, gengwu: Mars retrograded twenty-one days, crossing Dipper's southeast and southwest stars.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「月有賊臣。

translations.literal: Interpretation says: "The moon—there is a treacherous minister."
translations.idiomatic: The reading says: "The moon marks a treacherous minister."

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「人主無出，廊廟間有伏兵。

translations.literal: It is also said: "The ruler must not go out; there are hidden troops between corridor and temple."
translations.idiomatic: It also says: "The ruler must not leave the palace; hidden troops lurk in the corridors."

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「君死，有赦。

translations.literal: It is also said: "The ruler dies; there is amnesty."
translations.idiomatic: It also says: "The ruler dies; amnesty follows."

sentences.zh: 」後二年，少帝廢之應也。

translations.literal: Two years later—the response to deposing the young emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later came the deposing of the young emperor.

sentences.zh: 六月丙申，月犯亢。

translations.literal: Sixth month, bingshen day—the moon violated Neck.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth month, bingshen: the moon crossed Neck.

sentences.zh: 七月戊寅，月犯畢大星。

translations.literal: Seventh month, wuyin day—the moon violated the great star of Net.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh month, wuyin: the moon crossed Net's great star.

sentences.zh: 閏十月庚申，月犯牽牛。

translations.literal: Intercalary tenth month, gengshen day—the moon violated the Lead Ox.
translations.idiomatic: Intercalary tenth month, gengshen: the moon crossed the Lead Ox.

sentences.zh: 丙子，又犯左執法。

translations.literal: Bingzi day—it again violated the Left Law-enforcer.
translations.idiomatic: Bingzi: it crossed the Left Law-enforcer again.

sentences.zh: 十一月乙未，月食畢大星。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, yiwei day—lunar eclipse of Net's great star.
translations.idiomatic: Eleventh month, yiwei: lunar eclipse of Net's great star.

sentences.zh: 六年正月己亥，太白犯熒惑，相去二寸。

translations.literal: Sixth year, first month, jihai day—Venus violated Mars, about two cun apart.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth year, first month, jihai: Venus crossed Mars, about two cun apart.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「其野有兵喪，改立侯王。

translations.literal: Interpretation says: "In that region there is military mourning; marquis-kings are changed and enthroned."
translations.idiomatic: The reading says: "War and mourning in that quarter; marquis-kings are replaced."

sentences.zh: 」三月丁卯，日入後，眾星未見，有流星白色，大如斗，從太微間南行，尾長尺餘。

translations.literal: Third month, dingmao day—after sunset, before the multitude of stars appeared, a white meteor as large as a dou, from between the Supreme Palace southward, its tail over a chi long.
translations.idiomatic: Third month, dingmao: after sunset, before stars appeared, a white meteor the size of a dou shot south from the Supreme Palace, tail over a chi long.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「有兵與喪。

translations.literal: Interpretation says: "There is warfare and mourning."
translations.idiomatic: The reading says: "War and mourning follow."

sentences.zh: 」四月丁巳，月犯軒轅。

translations.literal: Fourth month, dingsi day—the moon violated the Chariot.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth month, dingsi: the moon crossed the Chariot.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「女主有憂。

translations.literal: Interpretation says: "The chief consort has sorrow."
translations.idiomatic: The reading says: "The chief consort faces sorrow."

sentences.zh: 」五月丁亥，太白犯軒轅。

translations.literal: Fifth month, dinghai day—Venus violated the Chariot.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth month, dinghai: Venus crossed the Chariot.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「女主失勢。

translations.literal: Interpretation says: "The chief consort loses power."
translations.idiomatic: The reading says: "The chief consort loses power."

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「四方禍起。

translations.literal: It is also said: "Calamity rises in the four directions."
translations.idiomatic: It also says: "Disaster rises on all sides."

sentences.zh: 」其後年，少帝廢，廢後慈訓太后崩。

translations.literal: In the following year the young emperor was deposed; after deposition Empress Dowager Cixun died.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the young emperor was deposed; afterward Empress Dowager Cixun died.

sentences.zh: 六月己未，月犯氐。

translations.literal: Sixth month, jiwei day—the moon violated Dipper.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth month, jiwei: the moon crossed Dipper.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，有彗長可丈餘。

translations.literal: Xinyou day—there was a comet over a zhang long.
translations.idiomatic: Xinyou: a comet over a zhang long appeared.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「陰謀奸宄起。

translations.literal: Interpretation says: "Secret plots and treachery rise."
translations.idiomatic: The reading says: "Secret plots and treachery arise."

sentences.zh: 」一曰：「宮中火起。

translations.literal: One account says: "Fire rises in the palace."
translations.idiomatic: Another account says: "Fire breaks out in the palace."

sentences.zh: 」後安成王錄尚書、都督中外諸軍事，廢少帝而自立，陰謀之應。

translations.literal: Afterward the Prince of Ancheng held the post of Recorder of the Secretariat and Director of All Armies at Home and Abroad, deposed the young emperor and enthroned himself—the response to secret plotting.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Prince of Ancheng, as chief minister and commander, deposed the young emperor and seized the throne—the fulfillment of secret plotting.

sentences.zh: 八月戊辰，月掩畢大星。

translations.literal: Eighth month, wuchen day—the moon masked the great star of Net.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth month, wuchen: the moon occulted Net's great star.

sentences.zh: 丙子，月與太白並，光芒相著，在太微西蕃南三尺所。

translations.literal: Bingzi day—the moon and Venus together, their lights touching, about three chi south of the western rampart of the Supreme Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Bingzi: the moon and Venus conjoined, lights touching, three chi south of the Supreme Palace's western rampart.

sentences.zh: 九月辛巳，熒惑犯左執法。

translations.literal: Ninth month, xinsi day—Mars violated the Left Law-enforcer.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth month, xinsi: Mars crossed the Left Law-enforcer.

sentences.zh: 癸未，太白犯右執法。

translations.literal: Guiwei day—Venus violated the Right Law-enforcer.
translations.idiomatic: Guiwei: Venus crossed the Right Law-enforcer.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，犯左執法。

translations.literal: Xinmao day—it violated the Left Law-enforcer.
translations.idiomatic: Xinmao: it crossed the Left Law-enforcer.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，月犯上相，太白犯熒惑。

translations.literal: Yisi day—the moon violated the Upper Minister; Venus violated Mars.
translations.idiomatic: Yisi: the moon crossed the Upper Minister; Venus crossed Mars.

sentences.zh: 其夜，月又犯太白。

translations.literal: That night, the moon again violated Venus.
translations.idiomatic: That night the moon crossed Venus again.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「其國內外有兵喪，改立侯王。

translations.literal: Interpretation says: "Within the state and without there is military mourning; marquis-kings are changed and enthroned."
translations.idiomatic: The reading says: "War and mourning at home and abroad; marquis-kings are replaced."

sentences.zh: 」明年，帝崩，又少帝廢之應也。

translations.literal: The next year the Emperor died—again the response to deposing the young emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the emperor died—again fulfilling the omen of the young emperor's deposition.

sentences.zh: 七年二月庚午，日無光，烏見。

translations.literal: Seventh year, second month, gengwu day—the sun had no light; crows appeared.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh year, second month, gengwu: the sun lost its light and crows appeared.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「王者惡之。

translations.literal: Interpretation says: "Kings detest it."
translations.idiomatic: The reading says: "Kings dread this omen."

sentences.zh: 」其日庚午，吳、楚之分野。

translations.literal: That day gengwu was the territorial division of Wu and Chu.
translations.idiomatic: That gengwu day fell in the Wu-Chu territorial division.

sentences.zh: 四月甲子，日有交暈，白虹貫之。

translations.literal: Fourth month, jiazi day—the sun had interlocking halos; a white rainbow pierced through.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth month, jiazi: the sun showed interlocking halos pierced by a white rainbow.

sentences.zh: 是月癸酉，帝崩。

translations.literal: That month, guiyou day, the Emperor died.
translations.idiomatic: That month, guiyou, the emperor died.

sentences.zh: 廢帝天康元年五月庚辰，月犯軒轅女禦大星。

translations.literal: Deposed Emperor, Tiankang first year, fifth month, gengchen day—the moon violated the great star of the Chariot Woman Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Deposed Emperor, Tiankang first year, fifth month, gengchen: the moon crossed the Chariot Woman Attendant's great star.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「女主憂。

translations.literal: Interpretation says: "The chief consort grieves."
translations.idiomatic: The reading says: "The chief consort grieves."

sentences.zh: 」後年，慈訓太后崩。

translations.literal: The following year, Empress Dowager Cixun died.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Empress Dowager Cixun died.

sentences.zh: 癸未，月犯左執法。

translations.literal: Guiwei day—the moon violated the Left Law-enforcer.
translations.idiomatic: Guiwei: the moon crossed the Left Law-enforcer.

sentences.zh: 光大元年正月甲寅，月犯軒轅大星。

translations.literal: Guangda first year, first month, jiayin day—the moon violated the great star of the Chariot.
translations.idiomatic: Guangda first year, first month, jiayin: the moon crossed the Chariot's great star.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「女主當之。

translations.literal: Interpretation says: "The chief consort will bear it."
translations.idiomatic: The reading says: "The chief consort will suffer for it."

sentences.zh: 」八月戊寅，月食哭星。

translations.literal: Eighth month, wuyin day—lunar eclipse of the Weeping star.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth month, wuyin: lunar eclipse of the Weeping star.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「有喪泣事。

translations.literal: Interpretation says: "There are mourning and weeping affairs."
translations.idiomatic: The reading says: "Mourning and weeping follow."

sentences.zh: 」明年，太后崩，臨海王薨，哭泣之應也。

translations.literal: The next year the Empress Dowager died and the Prince of Linhai died—the response to weeping.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the empress dowager and the Prince of Linhai died—the fulfillment of weeping omens.

sentences.zh: 壬午，鎮星辰星合於軫。

translations.literal: Renwu day—Saturn and the Chronos star conjoined in Chariot Shaft.
translations.idiomatic: Renwu: Saturn and the Chronos star conjoined in Chariot Shaft.

sentences.zh: 九月戊午，辰星太白相犯。

translations.literal: Ninth month, wuwu day—Mercury and Venus mutually violated each other.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth month, wuwu: Mercury and Venus crossed each other.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「改立侯王。

translations.literal: Interpretation says: "Marquis-kings are changed and enthroned."
translations.idiomatic: The reading says: "Marquis-kings are replaced."

sentences.zh: 」己未，月犯歲星。

translations.literal: Jwei day—the moon violated Jupiter.
translations.idiomatic: Jiwei: the moon crossed Jupiter.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「國亡君。

translations.literal: Interpretation says: "The state loses its ruler."
translations.idiomatic: The reading says: "The state loses its ruler."

sentences.zh: 」十二月辛巳，月又犯歲星。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, xinsi day—the moon again violated Jupiter.
translations.idiomatic: Twelfth month, xinsi: the moon crossed Jupiter again.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，月犯建星。

translations.literal: Xinmao day—the moon violated the Establishment star.
translations.idiomatic: Xinmao: the moon crossed the Establishment star.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「大人惡之。

translations.literal: Interpretation says: "The great man detests it."
translations.idiomatic: The reading says: "The great man dreads this omen."

translations.literal: (Closing quotation.)
translations.idiomatic: (This closes the omen text cited above.)

sentences.zh: 二年正月戊申，月掩歲星。

translations.literal: Second year, first month, wushen day—the moon masked Jupiter.
translations.idiomatic: Second year, first month, wushen: the moon occulted Jupiter.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「國亡君。

translations.literal: Interpretation says: "The state loses its ruler."
translations.idiomatic: The reading says: "The state loses its ruler."

sentences.zh: 」五月乙未，月犯太白。

translations.literal: Fifth month, yiwei day—the moon violated Venus.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth month, yiwei: the moon crossed Venus.

sentences.zh: 六月丙寅，太白犯右執法。

translations.literal: Sixth month, bingyin day—Venus violated the Right Law-enforcer.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth month, bingyin: Venus crossed the Right Law-enforcer.

sentences.zh: 壬子，客星見氐東。

translations.literal: Renzi day—a guest star appeared east of Dipper.
translations.idiomatic: Renzi: a guest star appeared east of Dipper.

sentences.zh: 八月庚寅，月犯太微。

translations.literal: Eighth month, gengyin day—the moon violated the Supreme Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth month, gengyin: the moon crossed the Supreme Palace.

sentences.zh: 九月庚戌，太白逆行，與鎮星合，在角。

translations.literal: Ninth month, gengxu day—Venus moved retrograde and conjoined with Saturn in Horn.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth month, gengxu: Venus retrograded and conjoined Saturn in Horn.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「為白衣之會。

translations.literal: Interpretation says: "This is a gathering of white-robed mourners."
translations.idiomatic: The reading says: "This marks a gathering of mourners in white."

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「所合之國，為亡地，為疾兵。

translations.literal: It is also said: "The state where they conjoin loses territory and faces plague armies."
translations.idiomatic: It also says: "The state where they meet loses land and faces plague armies."

sentences.zh: 」戊午，太白晝見。

translations.literal: Wuwu day—Venus visible by day.
translations.idiomatic: Wuwu: Venus appeared in daylight.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「太白晝見，國更政易王。

translations.literal: Interpretation says: "Venus visible by day—the state changes government and kings."
translations.idiomatic: The reading says: "Daylight Venus means regime change."

sentences.zh: 」十一月丙午，歲星守右執法，甲申，月犯太微東南星。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, bingwu day—Jupiter guarded the Right Law-enforcer; jiashen day, the moon violated the southeast star of the Supreme Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Eleventh month, bingwu: Jupiter guarded the Right Law-enforcer; jiashen, the moon crossed the Supreme Palace's southeast star.

sentences.zh: 戊子，太白入氐。

translations.literal: Wuzi day—Venus entered Dipper.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzi: Venus entered Dipper.

sentences.zh: 十二月甲寅，慈訓太后廢帝為臨海王，太建二年四月薨，皆其應也。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, jiayin day—Empress Dowager Cixun deposed the Emperor as Prince of Linhai; he died fourth month, Taijian second year—all these were the responses.
translations.idiomatic: Twelfth month, jiayin: Empress Dowager Cixun deposed the emperor as Prince of Linhai; he died in Taijian second year, fourth month—all as foretold.

sentences.zh: 宣帝太建七年四月丙戌，有星孛於大角。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan, Taijian seventh year, fourth month, bingxu day—a broom star appeared at the Great Horn.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan, Taijian seventh year, fourth month, bingxu: a broom star appeared at the Great Horn.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「人主亡。

translations.literal: Interpretation says: "The ruler perishes."
translations.idiomatic: The reading says: "The ruler perishes."

sentences.zh: 」五月庚辰，熒惑犯右執法。

translations.literal: Fifth month, gengchen day—Mars violated the Right Law-enforcer.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth month, gengchen: Mars crossed the Right Law-enforcer.

sentences.zh: 壬子，又犯右執法。

translations.literal: Renzi day—it again violated the Right Law-enforcer.
translations.idiomatic: Renzi: it crossed the Right Law-enforcer again.

sentences.zh: 十年二月癸亥，日上有背。

translations.literal: Tenth year, second month, guihai day—there was back-vapor above the sun.
translations.idiomatic: Tenth year, second month, guihai: back-vapor appeared above the sun.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「其野失地，有叛兵。

translations.literal: Interpretation says: "That region loses territory; there are rebel armies."
translations.idiomatic: The reading says: "Territory is lost; rebel armies rise."

sentences.zh: 」甲子，吳明徹軍敗于呂梁，將卒並為周軍所虜。

translations.literal: Jiazi day—Wu Mingche's army was defeated at Lüliang; officers and soldiers were all captured by the Zhou army.
translations.idiomatic: Jiazi: Wu Mingche's army was crushed at Lüliang; officers and men were captured by Zhou.

sentences.zh: 來年，淮南之地，盡沒于周。

translations.literal: The next year, the Huai River region was entirely lost to Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the entire Huai region fell to Zhou.

sentences.zh: 十月癸卯，月食熒惑。

translations.literal: Tenth month, guimao day—lunar eclipse of Mars.
translations.idiomatic: Tenth month, guimao: lunar eclipse of Mars.
